A.explanation: If $F$ is proportional to $v$, then $P = Fv$ must increase with $v$, so $P$ cannot stay constant.

B.explanation: If $F$ is proportional to $v$, then $P = Fv$ is proportional to $v \times v = v^2$, not to $v$.

C.explanation: If $F$ is proportional to $v^2$, then $P = Fv$ is proportional to $v^2 \times v = v^3$, not to $v^2$.

D.explanation: If $F$ is proportional to $v^2$, then $P = Fv$ is proportional to $v^2 \times v = v^3$, which is self-consistent.

hints: Notice the question states motion at constant speed, so the forward force must balance the resistive force $F$ and work is done against $F$.
Recall the power for a force moving at speed $v$ is $P = Fv$, so $P$ must contain one extra factor of $v$ compared with $F$.
Test each row by multiplying the given $F$ dependence by $v$: only a row where the $P$ power of $v$ is one higher than the $F$ power of $v$ can be possible.
walkthrough: Identify the physics: at constant speed $v$ the applied force equals the resistive force $F$, so power is work per unit time against $F$.
State the governing rule: $P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{Fx}{t} = Fv$ for motion in the direction of the force.
Apply proportionality: if $F$ is proportional to $v^n$, then $P$ is proportional to $v^n \times v = v^{n+1}$.
Check the $F$ proportional to $v^2$ case: $P$ must then be proportional to $v^2 \times v = v^3$.
Compare with the table: only the row with $F$ proportional to $v^2$ and $P$ proportional to $v^3$ satisfies $P = Fv$. This is option D.
